newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bank confirms Scotiabank interest.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bank confirms Scotiabank interest.

text.p: Argentina's Banco Quilmes said Thursday a newspaper report that Canada's Bank of Nova Scotia was interested in acquiring a majority stake in it was "generally" accurate.

"In general terms, the information is correct," Quilmes's executive vice president Gabriel Coqueugniot told the Buenos Aires Stock Exchange in a letter in reference to an interview published Wednesday.
Argentina's financial daily Cronista reported that Scotiabank was interested in increasing its holding in Quilmes to 50 percent plus one share. It was not clear what Scotiabank's current holding is.
But Coqueugniot denied that a letter of intent had been signed with Scotiabank as the report quoted him as saying.
"It's not correct ... that a letter of intent has been signed," Coqueugniot said.

"The (Quilmes) board has to this date not approved plans that I have submitted on the bank management's behalf," he said. "Neither has it expressed its opinion on a capital increase or on how it would be done."

Coqueugniot said the plan submitted to the board for the 1997-2000 period was aimed at taking advantage of growth opportunities the financial market offered, for which Quilmes would require a future capital increase.
Among the alternatives submitted to the board were a capital injection by "partners" and a listing shares in Quilmes.
Cronista reported that Quilmes' capital would be increased from $127 million to almost $190 million.

"With these funds, a growth plan for 12 to 18 months could be financed, but for year 2000, the idea is that Quilmes accumulate $400 million or $450 million in capital to be able to manage $4 billion in assets, twice as much as today," he was quoted by the newspaper as saying.
